correctness.rationale: For 2≤m≤n, 0≤t≤m and connected K_{m,n}−M_t (only (2,2,2) excluded), each blue vertex has either p or p−1 white cross-shore neighbors when p vertices of A are white; hence any p≥3 cannot decrease, and likewise q≤2 in any successful zero-forcing initial complement. For t=0, three whites cannot all be removed, while a two-white A/B pair is forceable. For t=1, the sole missing edge permits three but not four whites: with a (2,2) white profile, a first force must use the single deleted pair and subsequently strands two whites on the opposite shore. For t≥2, four whites are forceable by {a1,a2,b1,b3}, through b2→a1→b3→a2→b1 (interpreting the middle terms as successive forces), giving Z=m+n−2−min(t,2). Domination at the Z threshold is obtained by explicitly complementary white sets except (2,2,1), m=2,t=2,n≥3, and m=n=3,t∈{2,3}. In m=2,t=2, any Z-set has no selected A vertex, leaving two undominated B vertices; in m=n=3,t=2 or 3, any dominating A/B selected pair must have two white neighbors per selected vertex, so forcing cannot start. Presented Z+1 witnesses dominate and force in each exception. All proof witnesses and lower-bound regimes were checked independently. These are infinite proof arguments, not inferred from finite exhaustive runs.
residual_risks: Finite brute force is limited to 58 profiles; all-parameter validity depends on the reconstructed symbolic shore-count proof.
Matching-defect restriction is essential: general t deleted edges can remove two neighbors from one vertex and invalidate the p≥3 invariant.

scientific_claim: For connected G=K_{m,n}−M_t, 2≤m≤n, 0≤t≤m: Z(G)=m+n−2−min(t,2). The dom-forcing number F_d(G) equals Z(G)+1 precisely for (m,n,t)=(2,2,1), for m=2,t=2,n≥3, and for (m,n)=(3,3), t∈{2,3}; elsewhere F_d=Z.
scientific_limitations: No extension to arbitrary sets of removed edges is claimed.
Small-graph enumeration independently corroborates but does not replace the proof.
Previously known t=0 and isolated standard-graph cases are not claimed as separately novel.
Originality is a qualified best-of-knowledge judgment.

evidence: Susanth 2026 Theorem 5.8 establishes intact K_{m,n} as a baseline invariant family.
Explicit lower bounds and forcing chains isolate why matching deletion changes the maximum forceable white count from 2 to 3 to 4 and no further.
Exact obstruction classification shows when domination costs one additional selected vertex.
value.rationale: Simultaneous domination and zero forcing is a natural hybrid invariant, and complete bipartite graphs are one of its foundational exact families. Deleting a matching is a canonical degree-balanced sparse defect: it is not an arbitrary slice. The result gives the full sharp transition as defect size t changes (two unit decreases in Z and subsequent saturation), together with a complete three-regime equality/failure classification for F_d=Z including small-shore obstructions. This structural robustness law is useful for interpreting how zero-forcing dynamics interact with static domination after sparse edge failure, and goes materially beyond recomputing a known table. Its individual standard-graph examples and t=0 case are not claimed as separate new results.
residual_risks: The construction does not address arbitrary edge failures, propagation time, or connected dom-forcing.
The novelty of individual P4/C6/Q3 values is zero; the value arises from the full family classification.
